```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Sou et al. (2019) studied three PqsR-antagonist quorum-sensing inhibitors
(QSIs) under development for chronic *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* lung infection.
Each compound was given to rats by intratracheal (IT) instillation of a
solubilised dose, and plasma, lung-homogenate and (for SEN001 only)
bronchoalveolar-lavage (BAL) concentrations were modelled simultaneously in
NONMEM. The three compounds share one general structure (Figure 2 of the paper)
but have separate parameter estimates and different subsets of the
compartments, so they are packaged as three models:

* `Sou_2019_SEN001_rat`: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sou_2019_SEN001_rat"))$description`
* `Sou_2019_SEN019_rat`: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sou_2019_SEN019_rat"))$description`
* `Sou_2019_SEN032_rat`: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sou_2019_SEN032_rat"))$description`
* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sou_2019_SEN001_rat"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xphs.2018.09.017> (open access,
  PMC6307981)

The structures of SEN019 and SEN032 are not disclosed by the authors (patent
pending); SEN001 is 3-amino-7-chloro-2-nonylquinazolin-4(3H)-one.

# Population

Male Sprague-Dawley rats (Methods, "Pharmacokinetic Studies"; Table 2). SEN001
was studied at Laval University (Quebec, Canada) in 21 rats given 0.067 mg/kg,
with plasma, lung and BAL sampled at 0.5, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24 and 48 h. SEN019
(0.12 mg/kg) and SEN032 (0.28 mg/kg) were studied at XenoGesis / Saretius
(Nottingham, UK) in 18 rats each, with plasma and lung (no BAL) sampled at
0.167, 0.5, 1, 3, 6 and 24 h. Doses were limited by solubility and compound
availability and were delivered as a solution in PEG400 2% + polysorbate 80 2%
w/w in water (PP2%). Sampling was terminal, so the authors did not estimate
interindividual variability; data below the LLOQ were handled with the M3
method. Individual body weights are not reported, and the parameters are scaled
to a typical 0.3 kg rat.

The same information is available programmatically, e.g.
`readModelDb("Sou_2019_SEN001_rat")()$population`.

# Model structure

With `lung` the central lung compartment (dose site), `lung_deep` the deep lung
compartment, `central` plasma and `peripheral1` the peripheral tissue
compartment, Equations 1-4 of the paper are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{dA_L}{dt} &= -\frac{CL_{LP}}{V_L}A_L + \frac{CL_{LP}}{V_C}A_C - \frac{Q_L}{V_L}A_L + \frac{Q_L}{V_{LP}}A_{LP} \\
\frac{dA_C}{dt} &= \frac{CL_{LP}}{V_L}A_L - \frac{CL_{LP}}{V_C}A_C - \frac{CL_C}{V_C}A_C - \frac{Q_C}{V_C}A_C + \frac{Q_C}{V_P}A_P \\
\frac{dA_P}{dt} &= \frac{Q_C}{V_C}A_C - \frac{Q_C}{V_P}A_P \\
\frac{dA_{LP}}{dt} &= \frac{Q_L}{V_L}A_L - \frac{Q_L}{V_{LP}}A_{LP}
\end{aligned}
$$

`CL_LP` (`q_lung`) is a single clearance that moves drug both from lung to
plasma and back. SEN001 has the deep lung but no peripheral tissue compartment,
SEN019 has neither, and SEN032 has both (Results, "Pharmacokinetic Modeling";
Table 5 dashes).

For SEN001, BAL was collected before the lung was removed. The BAL
concentration is Equation 5, `Cbal = FBAL / VBAL * A_L`, and the lung
homogenate holds the amount the lavage did not recover,
`Clung_postbal = (1 - FBAL) * A_L / V_L` (Methods: "the total amount of drug in
the central lung compartment represents the sum of drug amounts in the BAL and
lung samples"). `Clung = A_L / V_L` is the lung concentration before lavage,
the quantity the authors simulated in Figure 4 and the quantity measured
directly for SEN019 and SEN032.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | SEN001 | SEN019 | SEN032 | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ODEs for `lung`, `central`, `peripheral1`, `lung_deep` | yes | yes | yes | Equations 1-4; Figure 2 |
| `Cbal = fbal / v_bal * lung` | yes | -- | -- | Equation 5 |
| `Clung_postbal = (1 - fbal) * lung / v_lung` | yes | -- | -- | Methods text after Equation 5; checked against Figure 3 below |
| `lq_lung` (CLLP, L/h) | 0.0175 | 0.0724 | 0.150 | Table 5 |
| `lv_lung` (VL, L, fixed) | 0.002 | 0.002 | 0.002 | Table 5; Methods (fixed to the 2 g rat lung) |
| `lcl` (CLC, L/h) | 0.0745 | 1.11 | 3.74 | Table 5 |
| `lvc` (VC, L) | 0.0855 | 0.583 | 1.51 | Table 5 |
| `lq` (QC, L/h) | -- | -- | 2.35 | Table 5 |
| `lvp` (VP, L) | -- | -- | 1.36 | Table 5 |
| `lq_lung_lung_deep` (QL, L/h) | 0.00596 | -- | 0.0107 | Table 5 |
| `lv_lung_deep` (VLP, L) | 0.0582 | -- | 0.00360 | Table 5 |
| `logitfbal` (FBAL) | logit(0.980) | -- | -- | Table 5 |
| `lv_bal` (VBAL, L, fixed) | 0.008 | -- | -- | Not printed; back-solved from Figure 3 (see below) |
| `propSd` (plasma) | 0.459 | 0.248 | 0.253 | Table 5, PROPPL |
| `addSd` (plasma, ug/L) | -- | sqrt(0.284) = 0.533 | sqrt(0.505) = 0.711 | Table 5, ADDPL (variance, footnote a) |
| `propSd_Clung` / `propSd_Clung_postbal` (lung) | 0.435 | 0.181 | 0.461 | Table 5, PROPLG |
| `propSd_Cbal` (BAL) | 0.380 | -- | -- | Table 5, PROPBAL |

```{r load-models}
mods <- list(
  SEN001 = readModelDb("Sou_2019_SEN001_rat"),
  SEN019 = readModelDb("Sou_2019_SEN019_rat"),
  SEN032 = readModelDb("Sou_2019_SEN032_rat")
)
# Parameters are for a typical 0.3 kg rat, so mg/kg doses become ug per rat.
rat_wt <- 0.3
study_dose_mgkg <- c(SEN001 = 0.067, SEN019 = 0.12, SEN032 = 0.28)
```

# Back-solving the BAL fluid volume

Equation 5 divides by `VBAL`, the volume of lavage fluid, but the paper does not
print it. It cancels from the ratio of the two SEN001 lung-side observations:

$$
\frac{C_{BAL}}{C_{lung,\,post\text{-}BAL}} = \frac{F_{BAL} \, V_L}{(1 - F_{BAL}) \, V_{BAL}}
$$

so `VBAL` follows from the observed BAL and lung medians at the same time,
without using the fitted absorption or disposition parameters. The maintainers
digitised the observed medians of Figure 3 (SEN001 lung and BAL panels, read
from the solid median lines on the log axis):

```{r vbal}
fig3_sen001 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~lung_obs, ~bal_obs,
  0.5,   2.76,      35,
  2,     0.44,      17,
  4,     0.71,      9.2,
  8,     0.21,      3.6,
  12,    0.19,      1.94,
  24,    0.108,     1.17,
  48,    0.0216,    0.26
)
fbal <- 0.980
v_lung <- 0.002
vbal_by_time <- fbal * v_lung / ((1 - fbal) * fig3_sen001$bal_obs / fig3_sen001$lung_obs)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(time_h = fig3_sen001$time, VBAL_mL = round(1000 * vbal_by_time, 1)),
  caption = "VBAL implied at each SEN001 sampling time (Figure 3 medians)."
)
median(vbal_by_time)
```

Six of the seven times imply 6-10 mL; the 2 h lung median (a dip below the
4 h value in Figure 3) is the outlier. The median, about 8 mL, is used:
`lv_bal <- fixed(log(0.008))`. A second route that does use the fitted model
(the typical-value lung amount against the observed BAL medians) is checked in
the next section. Users who know the lavage volume of their own protocol can
override `lv_bal`.

# Replicate Figure 3 (single intratracheal dose)

Figure 3 of the paper is a VPC of the final model. Because the model has no
interindividual variability, the VPC median is the typical-value prediction.
Below, the typical-value profile of each compound at its study dose is
compared with the observed medians the maintainers digitised from Figure 3.

```{r fig3-sim}
solve_typical <- function(compound, times) {
  dose_ug <- study_dose_mgkg[[compound]] * rat_wt * 1000
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_ug, cmt = "lung") |>
    rxode2::et(times, cmt = "central") |>
    as.data.frame()
  # Multiple `~` endpoints: observation rows need a dvid; dvid = 1 still
  # returns every algebraic output column.
  ev$dvid <- ifelse(ev$evid == 0, 1L, NA_integer_)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mods[[compound]], ev, returnType = "data.frame", useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::mutate(compound = compound)
}
grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0.05, 1, by = 0.05), seq(1.25, 6, by = 0.25), seq(7, 48, by = 1),
                      0.167, 0.5, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, 24, 48)))
typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  solve_typical("SEN001", grid),
  solve_typical("SEN019", grid[grid <= 6]),
  solve_typical("SEN032", grid[grid <= 6])
)
typ_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  typ |> dplyr::transmute(compound, time, matrix = "Plasma", conc = Cc),
  typ |> dplyr::filter(compound != "SEN001") |>
    dplyr::transmute(compound, time, matrix = "Lung", conc = Clung),
  typ |> dplyr::filter(compound == "SEN001") |>
    dplyr::transmute(compound, time, matrix = "Lung", conc = Clung_postbal),
  typ |> dplyr::filter(compound == "SEN001") |>
    dplyr::transmute(compound, time, matrix = "BAL", conc = Cbal)
)

fig3_obs <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(compound = "SEN001", matrix = "Plasma",
                 time = c(0.5, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, 48),
                 obs = c(185, 20, 11, 3.5, 2.3, 0.5, 0.24)),
  tibble::tibble(compound = "SEN001", matrix = "Lung",
                 time = fig3_sen001$time, obs = fig3_sen001$lung_obs),
  tibble::tibble(compound = "SEN001", matrix = "BAL",
                 time = fig3_sen001$time, obs = fig3_sen001$bal_obs),
  tibble::tibble(compound = "SEN019", matrix = "Plasma",
                 time = c(0.167, 0.5, 1, 3), obs = c(48.6, 24, 8.6, 0.256)),
  tibble::tibble(compound = "SEN019", matrix = "Lung",
                 time = c(0.167, 0.5, 1), obs = c(94, 33, 9.7)),
  tibble::tibble(compound = "SEN032", matrix = "Plasma",
                 time = c(0.167, 0.5, 1, 3), obs = c(33, 12, 5.5, 1.1)),
  tibble::tibble(compound = "SEN032", matrix = "Lung",
                 time = c(0.167, 0.5, 1), obs = c(100, 47, 14.6))
)
```

```{r fig3-plot, fig.height = 7}
ggplot(dplyr::filter(typ_long, conc > 1e-3), aes(time, conc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig3_obs, aes(time, obs), colour = "blue", shape = 1) +
  facet_wrap(compound ~ factor(matrix, levels = c("Plasma", "Lung", "BAL")),
             scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)",
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 3 of Sou 2019: lines are typical-value",
                       "predictions, circles the digitised observed medians.",
                       "SEN001 'Lung' is the homogenate collected after BAL."))
```

```{r fig3-check}
fig3_cmp <- fig3_obs |>
  dplyr::left_join(typ_long, by = c("compound", "matrix", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fold = pmax(conc / obs, obs / conc))
knitr::kable(
  fig3_cmp |>
    dplyr::mutate(conc = signif(conc, 3), fold = round(fold, 2)) |>
    dplyr::rename("Observed median (digitised)" = obs, "Typical prediction" = conc,
                  "Fold difference" = fold),
  caption = "Typical-value predictions against the observed medians of Figure 3 (ng/mL)."
)
gmfe <- exp(mean(abs(log(fig3_cmp$conc / fig3_cmp$obs))))
gmfe

# Second VBAL route: typical-value lung amount against the observed BAL medians.
vbal_model <- typ |>
  dplyr::filter(compound == "SEN001", time %in% fig3_sen001$time) |>
  dplyr::arrange(time) |>
  dplyr::mutate(vbal = fbal * lung / fig3_sen001$bal_obs)
1000 * median(vbal_model$vbal)
stopifnot(
  # Both VBAL routes land near the 8 mL used in the model.
  abs(1000 * median(vbal_model$vbal) - 8) < 1.5,
  abs(1000 * median(vbal_by_time) - 8) < 1.5
)
stopifnot(
  # Deterministic typical-value solve against medians of 3 rats per time; a
  # wrong clearance or volume (or reading the SEN001 lung homogenate as the
  # pre-lavage lung, a 50-fold shift) moves this far past 1.5.
  nrow(fig3_cmp) == 35,
  !anyNA(fig3_cmp$conc),
  gmfe < 1.5,
  max(fig3_cmp$fold) < 3
)
```

The largest differences are SEN001 plasma at 24 h and the SEN001 lung median at
2 h, where the three observed values per time scatter widely (Figure 3); the
typical prediction lies inside the paper's 95% confidence band of the predicted
median at both times. The SEN001 BAL points are not an independent check of the
BAL level, because `VBAL` was back-solved from them; they do check its time
course.

# Replicate Figures 4-6 (repeated dosing at 0.15 mg/kg)

The authors simulated 0.15 mg/kg (the mean study dose) every 24, 12 or 8 h for
24 h, with a log-normal interindividual variability of 30% CV on CLC only
(Equation 6), and summarised AUC over 24 h for lung (before lavage) and plasma.
The same exercise is repeated here with 100 virtual rats per compound and
interval. The IIV is added to each model for this simulation only; the packaged
models carry none, as the authors did not estimate it.

```{r rep-sim}
n_per_arm <- 100
dose_ug <- 0.15 * rat_wt * 1000
taus <- c(24, 12, 8)

add_cl_iiv <- function(mod) {
  mod |>
    rxode2::model(cl <- exp(lcl + etalcl)) |>
    rxode2::ini(etalcl ~ log(1 + 0.3^2))
}

make_regimen <- function(tau, id_offset) {
  dose_times <- seq(0, 24 - tau, by = tau)
  # Log-spaced sampling after every dose captures the very fast fall of the
  # lung concentration (SEN032 lung half-life is under a minute); the last
  # sample of each interval sits 1e-4 h before the next dose so the trough is
  # kept, and the grid ends exactly at 24 h.
  obs_times <- unlist(lapply(dose_times, function(d) {
    end <- if (d + tau >= 24) 24 else d + tau - 1e-4
    d + c(0, 10^seq(-4, log10(end - d), length.out = 60))
  }))
  obs_times <- sort(unique(round(pmin(obs_times, 24), 6)))
  one <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = dose_times, evid = 1L, amt = dose_ug, cmt = "lung", dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(time = obs_times, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  )
  tidyr::crossing(id = id_offset + seq_len(n_per_arm), one) |>
    dplyr::mutate(tau = tau) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190101)
rep_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(mods), function(cmpd) {
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(taus), function(i) {
    make_regimen(taus[i], id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
  }))
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
  rxode2::rxSolve(add_cl_iiv(mods[[cmpd]]), ev, keep = "tau",
                  returnType = "data.frame", useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::mutate(compound = cmpd) |>
    dplyr::select(compound, tau, id, time, Cc, Clung)
}))
rep_sim$arm <- paste0(rep_sim$compound, " q", rep_sim$tau, "h")
```

```{r fig4-5, fig.height = 7}
rep_long <- rep_sim |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Clung, Cc), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(matrix = dplyr::recode(matrix, Clung = "Lung", Cc = "Plasma"))

rep_long |>
  dplyr::group_by(compound, tau, matrix, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    lo = quantile(conc, 0.025), med = median(conc), hi = quantile(conc, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  # The paper's figures floor concentrations at 1e-3 ng/mL.
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(lo, med, hi), ~ pmax(.x, 1e-3))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(paste(matrix, "TAU", tau) ~ compound) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)",
       caption = paste("Replicates Figures 4 (lung) and 5 (plasma) of Sou 2019:",
                       "median and 95% prediction interval, 0.15 mg/kg every TAU h."))
```

## PKNCA: AUC over 24 h (Figure 6)

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- rep_long |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  # The solver returns values of order 1e-10 around zero once SEN019 and
  # SEN032 are cleared; they are numerical noise, not concentrations.
  dplyr::mutate(conc = pmax(conc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, matrix, id, time, conc)

nca_dose <- rep_sim |>
  dplyr::distinct(arm, tau, id) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(taus, function(t) {
      data.frame(tau = t, time = seq(0, 24 - t, by = t), amt = dose_ug)
    })),
    by = "tau", relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, id, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, conc ~ time | arm + matrix + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | arm + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE)
# SEN019 is fully cleared between doses, so its pre-dose troughs are zero.
# PKNCA's default drops zeros in the middle of a profile (treating them as
# BLQ), which would interpolate the next post-dose peak back across the whole
# dosing interval. These are model predictions, not BLQ data, so keep them.
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals,
  options = list(conc.blq = list(first = "keep", middle = "keep", last = "keep"))
))

auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, matrix) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean = mean(PPORRES), cv_pct = 100 * sd(PPORRES) / mean(PPORRES),
                   .groups = "drop")
```

The bar heights of Figure 6 (mean AUC0-24) were digitised by the maintainers.
Bars below about 50 ng*h/mL are only a few pixels tall, so their digitised
values carry an uncertainty of roughly +/-5 ng*h/mL.

```{r fig6-compare}
fig6 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,          ~matrix,  ~auclast,
  "SEN001 q24h", "Lung",   3011,
  "SEN019 q24h", "Lung",   669,
  "SEN032 q24h", "Lung",   295,
  "SEN001 q12h", "Lung",   5786,
  "SEN019 q12h", "Lung",   1319,
  "SEN032 q12h", "Lung",   630,
  "SEN001 q8h",  "Lung",   8521,
  "SEN019 q8h",  "Lung",   1968,
  "SEN032 q8h",  "Lung",   925,
  "SEN001 q24h", "Plasma", 595,
  "SEN019 q24h", "Plasma", 42,
  "SEN032 q24h", "Plasma", 14,
  "SEN001 q12h", "Plasma", 1133,
  "SEN019 q12h", "Plasma", 80,
  "SEN032 q12h", "Plasma", 24,
  "SEN001 q8h",  "Plasma", 1671,
  "SEN019 q8h",  "Plasma", 123,
  "SEN032 q8h",  "Plasma", 42
)
# Figure 6 plots means, so aggregate to the mean here; ncaComparisonTable()
# would otherwise summarise per-rat results by the median.
nca_mean <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, matrix, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(PPORRES = mean(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_mean,
  reference = fig6,
  by = c("arm", "matrix"),
  units = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste("Simulated mean AUC0-24 against Figure 6 of Sou 2019",
                  "(digitised). * differs from the reference by >20%.")
)
```

```{r fig6-check}
chk <- auc |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig6, by = c("arm", "matrix")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (mean - auclast) / auclast)
knitr::kable(
  chk |>
    dplyr::mutate(mean = signif(mean, 4), cv_pct = round(cv_pct, 1), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
    dplyr::rename("Arm" = arm, "Matrix" = matrix, "Simulated mean" = mean,
                  "Simulated CV (%)" = cv_pct, "Figure 6" = auclast, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff),
  caption = "AUC0-24 (ng*h/mL) and its between-rat CV."
)
big <- chk$auclast > 200
stopifnot(
  nrow(chk) == 18,
  # Bars tall enough to digitise to within a few percent. A wrong CLLP, CLC
  # or dose conversion moves these by tens of percent.
  abs(median(chk$pct_diff[big])) < 10,
  max(abs(chk$pct_diff[big])) < 20,
  # Results text: CLC variability gives a plasma AUC CV of 28.6-31.6% but a
  # lung AUC CV of only 1.2-5.3%. The plasma CV is a sample statistic over
  # 100 rats (standard error about 2 points), so the bounds are wide; the lung
  # bound still fails if lung exposure were driven by systemic clearance.
  all(chk$cv_pct[chk$matrix == "Plasma"] > 20),
  all(chk$cv_pct[chk$matrix == "Plasma"] < 40),
  all(chk$cv_pct[chk$matrix == "Lung"] < 10)
)
lung_mean <- setNames(chk$mean[chk$matrix == "Lung"], chk$arm[chk$matrix == "Lung"])
stopifnot(
  # Results: SEN019 and SEN032 every 8 h stay below SEN001 every 24 h (lung
  # AUC ratios about 1.5 and 3; lung CV is ~5%, so the margin is many SDs).
  lung_mean[["SEN001 q24h"]] > 1.2 * lung_mean[["SEN019 q8h"]],
  lung_mean[["SEN001 q24h"]] > 2 * lung_mean[["SEN032 q8h"]]
)
```

The simulation reproduces the paper's two conclusions: lung exposure to SEN019
and SEN032 dosed every 8 h stays below that to SEN001 dosed once daily (by
about 1.5- and 3-fold over 24 h), and the 30% variability in systemic clearance
passes almost entirely into plasma AUC while barely moving lung AUC.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **BAL fluid volume.** `VBAL` in Equation 5 is not reported. The maintainers
  back-solved it from the ratio of the digitised SEN001 BAL and lung medians in
  Figure 3 (median 8 mL across the seven sampling times, range of the six
  non-outlying times about 6-10 mL) and fixed `lv_bal` at 0.008 L. It affects
  only the `Cbal` output.
- **Lung homogenate after lavage.** The paper states that the central lung
  amount is the sum of the BAL and lung-sample amounts but prints only the BAL
  equation. The SEN001 lung-homogenate output is encoded as
  `(1 - FBAL) * A_L / V_L`; with `A_L / V_L` instead, the typical prediction
  would sit about 50-fold above the observed lung medians of Figure 3.
- **Residual error scales.** Footnote a of Table 5 says the additive errors are
  variances; they are converted to standard deviations
  (`addSd = sqrt(ADDPL)`). The proportional errors are reported in percent and
  read as CVs (`propSd = PROP / 100`).
- **FBAL scale.** Table 5 gives FBAL = 0.980 with unit "%", and the Discussion
  reads it as ">98%"; it is encoded as the fraction 0.980, on the logit scale so
  that it stays below 1 under refitting.
- **Body weight.** The parameters are reported for a 0.3 kg rat and no
  allometric exponent is given, so the models have no weight covariate. Give
  doses in ug per 0.3 kg rat (mg/kg x 0.3 x 1000).
- **Interindividual variability.** None was estimated (terminal sampling), so
  the packaged models have no etas. The 30% CV on CLC used for Figures 4-6 is
  the authors' simulation assumption (Equation 6) and is added in this vignette
  only.
- **BLQ handling.** The M3 likelihood used for data below the LLOQ affects
  estimation only and is not part of the packaged models.
- **Digitised targets.** Figure 3 medians and Figure 6 bar heights were read by
  the maintainers from the published raster figures; they carry
  pixel-resolution uncertainty of a few percent on the log (Figure 3) and
  linear (Figure 6) axes.
- No correction or erratum to the paper was found in Europe PMC (searched
  2026-11-25).
